scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: It starts raining, you open the app, and the same ride now costs almost double. But who decides that?

scenes.name: zones
scenes.text: The city is split into small hexagon zones, and each one is watched in real time.

scenes.name: demand
scenes.text: Demand is how many people are opening the app and requesting rides in that zone right now.

scenes.name: supply
scenes.text: Supply is how many drivers are free nearby. Rain, office rush, or a concert can flip the balance in minutes.

scenes.name: mult
scenes.text: When requests far outnumber drivers, an algorithm sets a multiplier for that zone, like one point five times.

scenes.name: fare
scenes.text: Your price is the normal fare, based on distance and time, scaled up by that multiplier. In India, rules cap it at two times the base fare.

scenes.name: balance
scenes.text: Higher prices pull drivers into the zone, and some riders wait. As things balance, the multiplier drops.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Riders, drivers, zone, multiplier. Price as a signal. Follow for more on how things really work.
